traceability.notes:
All acceptance criteria and requirements from docs/stories/006.0-DEV-FILE-VALIDATION.story.md are implemented and verified:
- Core functionality (validating that @story paths refer to existing .story.md files) is implemented in src/rules/valid-story-reference.ts, using storyReferenceUtils.ts for filesystem-aware existence checks, enforcing the .story.md extension by default, and handling annotation parsing. - Quality standards and safe filesystem handling are satisfied by centralized, cached checks in storyReferenceUtils.ts that never throw; all filesystem errors are converted to structured statuses and surfaced as ESLint diagnostics (fileMissing vs fileAccessError) in the rule. - Integration with annotation format validation (Story 005.0) is honored by focusing this rule on semantic reference validation over already-parsed @story annotations discovered via context.getSourceCode().getAllComments(). - User experience criteria are met via clear, specific error messages that include the offending path and distinguish between missing files, invalid extensions, invalid/unsafe paths, and filesystem access errors. Tests assert messageIds and embedded error text. - Error-handling and edge-case behavior (permissions errors, I/O failures, misconfigured directories, network-drive-like scenarios) are explicitly tested using Jest mocks of fs.existsSync and fs.statSync, ensuring the rule reports fileAccessError rather than crashing and that storyExists remains non-throwing. - Path resolution, security validation, project boundary enforcement, caching, and configurable story directories/options are implemented and thoroughly covered by tests and documentation. The rule supports `storyDirectories`, `allowAbsolutePaths`, and `requireStoryExtension` options, while still enforcing that any resolved files remain within the project root.
Given the concrete implementation, focused tests tied to this story and its REQ- identifiers, and matching documentation, the 006.0-DEV-FILE-VALIDATION story is fully implemented and passes.
